lead.small: Hours in the city of seven hills

lines.text: The tasca revival: where Lisbon really eats
Fado, rooftops & the best late-night ginjinha

pages.heading: Get lost on purpose
body: Lisbon does not announce itself. It reveals itself slowly: a tiled facade catching the afternoon sun, a tram bell somewhere below, the smell of grilled sardines drifting up a staircase that seems to lead nowhere in particular.

We came for a long weekend and kept finding reasons to stay. This guide is the route we wish someone had handed us at the airport: unhurried, a little steep, and full of places where the person behind the counter remembers your order by the second visit.

Inside you will find three neighbourhoods worth a whole day each, a list of tables we would cross the city for, and the quiet viewpoints that still feel like secrets. Wear good shoes. Say obrigado. And when the light turns gold an hour before sunset, climb something.
pages.quote: The best table in Lisbon is the one you weren't looking for.

pages.heading: Lisbon at a glance
tips: Buy a rechargeable Viva Viagem card at any metro station.
Shops close early on Sundays; plan lunch accordingly.
The light is best an hour before sunset. Climb something.

pages.heading: Alfama
pages.deck: Laundry lines, fado and the oldest streets in the city.
pages.story: The oldest district survived the 1755 earthquake and shows it: a maze of whitewashed lanes, laundry strung between balconies, and fado spilling from doorways after dark. Come early, before the tour groups, and walk downhill. Every staircase rewards you with a slice of river, and every corner seems to hide a tiny tasca with three tables and a grandmother at the stove.
pages.quote: Every staircase rewards you with a slice of river.

places.name: Miradouro das Portas do Sol
places.note: Terracotta rooftops to the river. Bring a coffee.

places.name: Sé de Lisboa
places.note: Romanesque cathedral, free to enter the nave.

places.name: Casa dos Bicos
places.note: A facade studded with stone diamonds.

pages.heading: Chiado
pages.deck: Poets and bookshops by day; Bairro Alto's street party by night.
pages.story: Poets, bookshops and the grand cafés of Chiado give way, after sunset, to the beautifully chaotic street party of Bairro Alto next door. Same hill, two personalities. Spend the afternoon browsing first editions and taking your coffee standing at the bar, then follow the crowd uphill when the shutters come down and the bars spill out onto the cobbles.

places.name: Livraria Bertrand
places.note: The world's oldest operating bookshop, since 1732.

places.name: A Brasileira
places.note: Order a bica beside the bronze poet.

places.name: Carmo Convent
places.note: A Gothic nave open to the sky.

places.name: Miradouro de São Pedro
places.note: Quiet garden terrace, great at dusk.

pages.heading: Belém
pages.deck: The age of discovery, carved in stone along the river.
pages.story: Lisbon's age of discovery in stone: monasteries, towers and a monument to the navigators, all along a breezy riverside promenade. Go on a weekday morning, start with the cloister before the coaches arrive, and save the custard tarts for the walk back. The light off the Tagus here is wide and silver, a different city from the narrow lanes uphill.
pages.quote: The light off the Tagus here is wide and silver.

places.name: Jerónimos Monastery
places.note: Manueline masterpiece; book the cloister online.

places.name: Pastéis de Belém
places.note: The original custard tart, warm, with cinnamon.

places.name: Belém Tower
places.note: Climb for river views; queues build after 11.

places.name: MAAT
places.note: A curved roof you can walk at sunset.

places.name: Padrão dos Descobrimentos
places.note: Lift to the top for the whole bay.

pages.heading: Eat & Drink
pages.deck: Six tables we would cross the city for.

items.name: Time Out Market
items.note: Chef stalls under one roof. Good for indecision.

items.name: Cervejaria Ramiro
items.note: Tiger prawns, then a steak sandwich to finish.

items.name: Manteigaria
items.note: Watch the tarts come out of the oven.

items.name: Ginjinha Sem Rival
items.note: A shot of cherry liqueur, standing.

items.name: Taberna da Rua das Flores
items.note: Small plates, daily blackboard, no bookings.

pages.note: Hours and prices change often. Verify before you go.

pages.heading: Ride the 28
pages.body: Tram 28 rattles through Graça, Alfama, Baixa and Estrela on a route older than most countries' railways. Board at Martim Moniz at 8am to get a seat and an empty street, sit on the right-hand side, and let the city tilt past the window.
pages.caption: Yellow trams, steep gradients, zero hurry.

gems.name: Jardim da Estrela at 8am
gems.note: Locals walk dogs under the palms. No one else is awake.

gems.name: Ler Devagar
gems.note: A bookshop inside a former printing works, with a flying bicycle.

gems.name: Senhora do Monte
gems.note: The highest viewpoint in the city and the least crowded.

gems.name: Pensão Amor
gems.note: A former brothel turned cocktail bar. Velvet and mischief.

stops.text: Walk up to Alfama via the Sé

sections.title: Getting around
items: Metro is fast and cheap; trams are for fun.
Uber and Bolt are inexpensive after dark.
Wear flat shoes: the cobbles are slippery.

sections.title: Money
items: Table snacks (couvert) are charged only if eaten.

sections.title: Etiquette
items: Greet shopkeepers: bom dia, boa tarde.
Keep voices low on trams and in churches.
